failure_summary.description: One trajectory passed a state abbreviation as a city; the other encoded a requested rating threshold as a one-item list.
Both trajectories omitted saving the exact search or filter result; the restaurant refinement also retrieved the older base result instead of the latest compatible result.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly requires correct state/city mapping, retrieving the latest compatible cache result, and saving every tool result, so repeating those rules would not patch a documentation gap. The rating failure exposes ambiguity in how to encode an unqualified requested rating; clarify threshold versus exact-value encoding.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an explicitly exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list or widen an exact value. For hotel and restaurant ratings on a 0–5 scale, interpret a requested rating threshold—including an unqualified request for options with an x-star rating—as a minimum `[x, 5]`, unless the user explicitly asks for exactly x; encode “at most x” as `[0, x]`. Follow the schema for other bounds and do not invent endpoints.
